questions.explain: Helpful comments ask for evidence or action and focus on the work. Unhelpful ones are vague or personal.

items.text: Which test covers the empty-input case?

items.misconception: Judge the change, not the tool. Say what is wrong with it.

items.text: This is too large to review properly. Could you split it by feature?
items.misconception: Asking for a reviewable size is legitimate and actionable.
It invites a reassurance, not evidence.

questions.prompt: In a diff, a test's expected value changed from 60 to 20 in the same commit that fixed a function. What is the best reviewer response?
questions.explain: A test edited to match new output may mean the test was weakened to pass. Ask why the expected value changed.

options.text: Ask why the value changed and what independent source says 20 is right
Approve, because the tests pass and the function was clearly fixed
options.misconception: Tests that were edited to pass do not show the function is correct.

options.text: Ask them to put the value back to 60, since tests must never be edited
options.misconception: Tests can legitimately change when the expected behaviour changes. What matters is an independent reason for the new value.

questions.prompt: Which notebook format is easier for a reviewer to diff?
questions.explain: A notebook stored as plain Python text shows the changed lines. A JSON notebook with outputs produces noisy diffs.

options.text: A plain .py notebook such as marimo

options.misconception: It is JSON with outputs and run counts, so diffs are noisy.
The storage format decides how readable a diff is.

questions.prompt: A reviewer asks you to explain why a branch exists, and you cannot. What does that tell you?
questions.explain: A fair question that you cannot answer means you do not yet understand your own change.

options.text: You are not ready to send it, so go and understand or remove it
The reviewer is asking about something that does not matter much
options.misconception: Explaining the reason for a line is an ordinary expectation of any author.

options.text: Paste in the agent's explanation of the branch without checking it
options.misconception: A justification written after the fact may not reflect why the code exists, and you still have not checked it.
